headline: Change is not a feature of the universe—it is the universe
universal_truth: Nothing permanent exists; flow is the fundamental nature of reality
fun_facts: Every atom in your body is replaced over about 7 years—you're literally not the same person
The Greek philosopher Heraclitus said 'you cannot step into the same river twice'—2,500 years ago
Even 'permanent' structures like mountains are slowly changing, just on timescales we can't perceive
discussion_questions: What change are you resisting that might be inevitable?
How has a painful change eventually led to something good?
If everything changes, what does that mean for how you live today?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Look at your hand. Every atom in it will be replaced over the next several years. The cells in your stomach lining? Replaced in days. You are not a thing—you are a process, constantly renewing. Change is not what happens to you. Change is what you are.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We crave stability, permanence, something solid to hold onto. But physics, biology, and philosophy all tell the same story: nothing lasts. So why do we suffer so much over change? And how can we make peace with impermanence?
cliff.prompt: How can we accept that everything changes?

options.text: By releasing attachment to how things 'should' stay
options.response: Yes. Suffering comes from clinging to what is inherently temporary.

options.text: By focusing on what remains relatively stable
options.response: Finding stability helps, but even stable things eventually change...

q1.title: You Are New
q1.script: Your body replaces billions of cells daily. Your skeleton is completely renewed every 10 years. Your taste buds last about 2 weeks. The 'you' from 7 years ago shares almost no physical matter with the you today. You are continuity without permanence.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "You Are New"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Heraclitus Was Right
q2.script: 2,500 years ago, Heraclitus said: 'You cannot step into the same river twice—for it is not the same river, and you are not the same person.' Ancient wisdom that modern physics confirms. Reality is flux masquerading as substance.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Mountain Time
q3.script: Mountains seem eternal, but they're eroding constantly—just slowly. The Himalayas rise about 5 millimeters per year. Even continents drift. There is nothing permanent in the universe—only different timescales of change.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Fighting change is fighting reality. The art of living is learning to flow with impermanence—to hold things lightly, love fully, and release gracefully. Everything you love will change. Love it anyway.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 30—one month of learning together. What a journey so far! Tomorrow, we'll discover how the sun powers all life on Earth. Until then, embrace change—it's the only constant.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Impermanence Practice - Letting Go
growTrack.learning_objective: Practice acceptance of change through reflection
growTrack.activity: Think of something you're holding onto that's already changing or gone—a relationship, a phase of life, an old version of yourself. Write a short letter saying goodbye to it. Thank it for what it gave you. Then, symbolically release it.
